Greek religion starts with Gaya and Chaos giving birth to gods; Ga marries Uranus, who dislikes his children and beats them up. These children rebel with their mother's help, and Cronis kills Uranus. Uranus then marries Rhea, and Cronis becomes king but fears rebellion. He eats his children, Rhea gives birth to Zeus secretly on an island. Zeus grows up and poisons Cronis, becoming the ultimate king.

This myth influences major historical figures like Akid, Ramis, Reheis, King David, and Genghis Khan. There are three layers: animistic creation of humans, Cronis's rebellion, and foreign mercenaries becoming kings due to their talent but overthrowing them for legitimacy. The Song dynasty founder was such a figure, needing myths to legitimize his rule.

In the beginning, the high priestess has a consort who establishes an elite; this makes people unhappy, leading one prince or son to form a political faction, slaying the consort and marrying the high priestess. This follows mythological patterns, and after the warlord dies, another cycle begins.
